subject: Voyager golden record
title: The Record Leaving Our Solar System Comes With a Uranium Clock

scenes.text: Two records are leaving the solar system, with a clock built into the cover.
In 1977, both Voyager probes launched carrying a 12-inch gold-plated copper record.
On it: 115 images, greetings in 55 languages and about 90 minutes of music.
The cover shows how to play it, and a map of 14 pulsars pointing to our Sun.
The clock is a speck of pure uranium-238. Measure how much has decayed, and you know how long it's been flying.
Its half-life is four and a half billion years. The record should last more than a billion.

description:
Voyager 1 and 2 each carry a 12-inch gold-plated copper record with 115 images, greetings in 55 languages and about 90 minutes of music, chosen by a committee chaired by Carl Sagan.
The cover carries playing instructions, a pulsar map locating the Sun and an ultra-pure uranium-238 source that works as a radioactive clock (half-life 4.51 billion years).
What song would you put on it today?
thumbnail_text: A URANIUM CLOCK ON A RECORD
first_comment: The record even includes a cartridge and needle to play it. Which song would you send to aliens?
